hero.h1.a: What your team says becomes what your team knows.
hero.h1.b: Never lose a spoken decision again.
hero.h1.c: The team mic that never needs a record button.
hero.sub: R1 plugs into your Mac and stays on through the workday. It recognizes your teammates by voice, captures the decisions, to-dos and key facts you say out loud, and sends them to the tools and Agents your team already uses — no one has to press record.
hero2.h2: No one presses record. Nothing slips through.
hero2.sub: Two-minute desk chats, the words before and after a meeting, a quick “I’ll take it” at standup — R1 follows your Mac from desk to meeting room, so the conversations that move work forward get captured.
value.h2: The most useful things your team knows are said, not written.
value.lead: Decisions are made in passing, tasks are claimed out loud, context is shared at the desk. R1 captures it without anyone pressing record — and turns it into something your team can use.

value.1.p: What gets decided out loud is written down automatically, with who said it and when.
value.2.p: What people promise turns into tasks with an owner and a due date, instead of being forgotten after the conversation.
value.3.p: No notes tool to open, nothing to write up afterwards, no re-briefing your Agents.
value.4.p: Everything lands in your Rutta team knowledge base and flows on to your docs, task tools and Agents. It always belongs to your team.
value.5.p: R1 is designed to process only enrolled teammates, and only at work. Lunch, hallways and private time are out of scope.
detail.always.body: No start button, no battery. Plugged into your Mac, R1 is on whenever your Mac is — so the small conversations that move work forward finally get captured.
detail.voice.body: Each teammate enrolls their voice once. R1 knows who said what — that’s how every task gets an owner — and is designed to discard voices it doesn’t recognize.
detail.flow.body: Confirmed notes land in your Rutta team knowledge base, then flow to the docs, task tools, chat apps and AI Agents you already use via MCP, API and CLI.
sc.h2: Built for the conversations no one records.
sc.lead: Nobody opens a recorder for a two-minute chat — yet that’s where dates move, tasks get claimed and context is shared. Built for co-located teams of 3–15.
sc.1.quote: “Let’s push launch from Dec 3 to Dec 10.”
sc.1.p: Minutes later, both of you get a note to confirm. One tap, and the project plan, related tasks and teammates are all updated — nobody writes a word.
sc.1.out.v: Launch date updated Dec 3 → Dec 10 · 3 dependent tasks shifted · teammates notified.
sc.2.h: Every “I’ll take it” gets an owner
sc.2.p: R1 knows who said it, so the task lands in your tracker with an owner and a due date — a reminder on Monday, and closed when someone says it’s sent.
sc.2.out.v: Send revised quote · Owner matched by voiceprint · Reminder set for Monday 9:00 AM.
sc.3.quote: “Let’s go with B — the client needs SSO first.”
sc.3.h: The why stays with the decision
sc.3.p: The real reasoning often happens as a meeting wraps up. R1 keeps it next to the decision, so it’s there when someone asks later.
sc.3.out.v: Selected Option B · Reason: Enterprise client requires SSO before pilot rollout.
sc.4.p: Teammates who weren’t in the room, and people who just joined, can look up what was decided, by whom, and why.
sc.4.out.v: Every confirmed decision carries speaker, timestamp and context — ready for anyone who joins later.
sc.5.quote: “Can you take the onboarding flow this week?”
sc.5.p: What you hand out in person is tracked automatically — no more saying it once at the desk and again in the group chat with an @.
sc.5.out.v: Onboarding flow assigned · Owner confirmed · Visible in team workspace and tracker.
sc.6.h: Your Agents are already up to date
sc.6.p: Confirmed decisions reach your Agents directly, so they can draft docs, create tasks and update plans without anyone re-briefing them.
sc.6.out.v: Your coding, doc and planning Agents query confirmed team decisions directly — zero manual copy-paste.
wf.h2: Plug it in once. Your team just keeps working.
wf.1.p: Plug R1 into your Mac. It’s on whenever your Mac is.
wf.2.p: Each teammate records a short voice sample once. Leave anytime.
wf.3.p: Talk at your desk or in the meeting room. Nothing to start or stop.
wf.4.p: Only the people in the conversation see the note first. Once someone confirms, it goes to the team.
wf.5.p: Decisions go to your knowledge base, tasks to your tracker with owners, and Agents can look it all up.
wf.apps: Designed to connect via MCP, API and CLI to the tools and Agents you already use

pv.h2: Always on — only for the people who opted in.
pv.lead: R1 is built for work, at your desk and in the meeting room. These are the privacy principles we’re designing around — not built yet.
pv.cap.ready: Green breathing light · R1 is ready.
pv.cap.input: Solid amber light · R1 is capturing enrolled teammates.
pv.cap.mute: Light off · an orange marker shows it’s physically muted.
pv.1.h: People in the conversation see it first
pv.1.p: Notes are visible only to the people who spoke. Nothing reaches the team until one of them shares it.
pv.2.p: Designed to keep only enrolled teammates’ speech. Visitors and others are discarded — not transcribed, not saved.
pv.3.p: Admins can manage members and settings, but can’t access recordings.
pv.4.h: Physical mute and a visible light
pv.4.p: A real switch on the side, and a light everyone at the table can see.
pv.5.p: Audio is processed on your Mac and not uploaded — only text from enrolled teammates syncs. Anyone can delete records they’re in.
pv.6.p: Your team’s content is never used to train AI models.

price.h2: Here’s what we’re thinking about price.
price.p: We’re not selling anything yet — no payment, no pre-orders. We share a test price so you can tell us honestly whether R1 is worth it for your team.
faq.1.a: Not yet. R1 is a concept — what you see are renders and illustrative scenarios, and there’s no prototype yet. We’re talking with teams first to decide whether to build it.
faq.2.q: Will there be an app and an admin console?
faq.2.a: Yes. R1 is designed to work with the Rutta app and team workspace — where teammates enroll their voice, review and confirm notes and browse team knowledge, and where admins manage members, permissions and integrations. Like R1, it’s still in the concept stage.
faq.3.q: What about visitors or people who haven’t joined?
faq.3.a: R1 compares each voice with enrolled teammates’ voiceprints. Our design goal is that voices it doesn’t recognize are discarded — not transcribed, not saved. Very short phrases and larger teams are still being worked on.
faq.4.q: Why hardware instead of just a Mac app?
faq.4.a: A Mac app can stop when the screen locks, keeps the system recording indicator on all day, and can fight other apps for the microphone. Plugged into USB-C, R1 stays powered and on only while you’re working at your Mac.
faq.5.a: First into your Rutta team knowledge base, then out to the docs, task tools, chat apps and Agents your team already uses — via MCP, API and CLI. It always belongs to your team.
faq.6.q: What happens after I sign up?
faq.6.a: We’ll email occasional updates. If your team is 3–15 people working side by side, we may invite you to a 15-minute chat — by video, phone or email — about the last decision your team had to chase down.

dlg.1: What we collect: only what you submit — your email, scenario, optional name, team size and notes, and optional survey answers — plus campaign parameters (UTM/ref) and locale/timezone if present.
dlg.2: How we use it: only to share R1 updates and, if you agree, to invite you to a short research chat. We never sell or rent your information.
dlg.3: R1 privacy principles (concept): participants confirm notes before they’re shared; only enrolled voices are kept; admins can’t access raw audio; physical mute switch and status light; audio is processed on your Mac; team content is never used to train models.
dlg.4: Unsubscribe & deletion: every email has a one-click unsubscribe link, and you can ask us to delete your record at any time.
